_meta.purpose: A seeded, sourced catalogue of tsunamis that struck or reached the Indian coast and the wider Indian Ocean / Arabian Sea. There is no reliable free REAL-TIME tsunami API to embed, so tsunamis are shown as a documented historical record; the live-hazard signal comes from the earthquake tracker's USGS `tsunami:1` flag and the official warning centre (INCOIS) linked in the page.
_meta.honesty: Death tolls for tsunamis vary widely by source (confirmed vs incl. missing). We give a representative figure with a range note and cite it. India-specific tolls are separated from the total where known.

sources.label: INCOIS — Indian Tsunami Early Warning System, tsunami history
Rastogi & Jaiswal (2006), 'A catalog of tsunamis in the Indian Ocean', Sci. Tsunami Hazards 25(3):128-143

_meta.fields: year, name, source_quake_mw, epicentre [lat,lng], deaths_total, deaths_india, india_impact, run_up_m (max wave height), note, source

tsunamis.name: 2004 Indian Ocean (Sumatra–Andaman) tsunami
tsunamis.india_impact: Tamil Nadu (8,009), Andaman & Nicobar (~1,310 confirmed, ~5,600 missing), Puducherry (599), Kerala (177), Andhra Pradesh (107). ~600,000 displaced in India.
tsunamis.note: The deadliest tsunami in recorded history, from a Mw 9.1-9.3 megathrust rupture off Sumatra. ~230,000 dead across 15 countries. India's confirmed toll ~12,405; some sources give up to ~18,045 incl. missing. Triggered the creation of the Indian Ocean Tsunami Warning System (INCOIS, 2007).

source.label: Britannica; Govt of India reports; Wikipedia — Effect on India

tsunamis.name: 1945 Makran tsunami (Arabian Sea)
tsunamis.india_impact: ~2 m waves at Mumbai (Bombay); boats torn from moorings and casualties reported; noticed as far south as the Karwar coast, Karnataka; up to ~15 m in the Gulf of Cambay.
tsunamis.note: The largest instrumentally-recorded tsunami of the NW Indian Ocean, from a Mw ~8.1 rupture on the Makran subduction zone. Killed up to ~4,000 (UNESCO cites ~300); Pasni and Ormara (now Pakistan) worst hit. A benchmark case for Arabian-Sea tsunami hazard to Gujarat/Maharashtra.

source.label: UNESCO; Rastogi & Jaiswal 2006; NHESS (2021) Makran study

tsunamis.name: 1883 Krakatoa tsunami
tsunamis.india_impact: Volcanic (not tectonic); waves recorded on tide gauges as far as Aden and the Indian coast. Minimal Indian casualties but a documented Indian Ocean-wide signal.
tsunamis.note: Caused by the cataclysmic eruption/collapse of Krakatoa in the Sunda Strait; ~36,000 killed, mostly in Java and Sumatra. Included as a major Indian-Ocean tsunami of non-earthquake origin.

source.label: Rastogi & Jaiswal 2006; Wikipedia — 1883 eruption of Krakatoa

tsunamis.name: 1762 Arakan (Bengal coast) tsunami
tsunamis.india_impact: The great Arakan earthquake off the Bengal/Myanmar coast raised the coastline and generated a tsunami felt along the eastern Bengal coast (present Bangladesh / West Bengal). Contemporary accounts describe the Hooghly disturbed at Kolkata.
tsunamis.note: A large ~Mw 8.5 megathrust event on the Arakan segment; permanent coastal uplift recorded. Toll uncertain (chronicle-level).

source.label: Rastogi & Jaiswal 2006, catalog of Indian Ocean tsunamis

tsunamis.name: 1881 Car Nicobar tsunami
tsunamis.india_impact: A Mw ~7.9 earthquake near Car Nicobar generated a tsunami recorded on tide gauges along the Indian east coast (Chennai/Madras) — an early instrumentally-observed Indian tsunami.
tsunamis.note: Low casualties but historically important as one of the earliest tide-gauge-recorded tsunamis in the region.
